verdicts.notes: Our own painterly drawing, not the donor: donor_single.png is a set of flat purple-black curved spikes; the variant is a different plant (a tuft of twisted olive and mauve leaves with perforated tips and yellow-green bulbs), so E1 is met. Painterly shading with no drawn keyline; the edges are soft and slightly darker, with no black outline (B1, B1a). Real alpha: composited on brown and on magenta at x4, there is no backdrop, halo or ground shadow; the base sits at the canvas bottom, bbox x 6-120, y 3-125 of 128 (D3, D4). Canvas 128 px for engine-default drawSize 1 (D2). At 32 px/cell (playzoom_single.png, 19 px quad) and in scale_single.png, the tufts read as olive/yellow over purple, apart from the brown ground by hue; it is a small plant, but it is not grey mud (B2, advisory). Its size beside the human in scale_single.png is right for a ground plant at 0.6 cells. The sickly olive, mauve and pustule look suits 'a pollution plant: Better not eat this'. There is no owner keep, no note, no sibling and no canon, per subject.json.

proposals: Plants: the brief has no line on whether a plant is judged as one picture or at its maxMeshCount cluster density. scale_single.png shows this one as a 3x3 cluster at maxMeshCount 9, where the bulbs repeat as a pattern. A line naming which view decides legibility would remove the ambiguity (evidence: subject.json size.maxMeshCount 9; scale_single.png).
